description: Signature database for public profile-page probes. Data, not code: edit this file to add or fix a site, then run `d3ta1l3r calibrate --sites <id>` before trusting it.

provenance.how_to_verify: d3ta1l3r calibrate --sites <id>   # probes a handle that cannot exist, and optionally one that does: d3ta1l3r calibrate --expect-hit <id>=your_handle
provenance.honesty_note: These signatures were authored by hand and are NOT live-verified against the sites. Sites change layout without notice, which is why an ambiguous response is reported as an error (unknown) and never as a hit. Detector semantics: 'marker' requires a found_marker; 'absence' means HTTP 200 plus a known not-found phrase; 'status' is a plain 404/200 heuristic and may not claim better than medium confidence.

sites.name: Steam
sites.not_found_marker: The specified profile could not be found.
sites.notes: Steam's error page is served with HTTP 200 and a very stable phrase, which makes the absence detector reliable. Vanity URLs only; numeric SteamID profiles are not covered.

sites.name: Wikipedia (user page)
sites.not_found_marker: does not have a user page with this exact name
sites.notes: MediaWiki serves the 'no such user page' notice with HTTP 200; the absence detector is exact here. A present user page does not imply recent activity.

sites.name: Duolingo

sites.name: Goodreads
sites.notes: Unverified signature; Goodreads sometimes answers 200 for unknown profiles. Calibrate before trusting.

sites.name: X (Twitter)
sites.notes: Disabled by default: X requires a signed-in session for profile pages and blocks anonymous scripted clients. Check your profile manually while signed in.

sites.name: Facebook
sites.notes: Disabled by default: Facebook serves a login wall to anonymous clients and its ToS prohibits automated access. Use the platform's own 'View as public' tool.

sites.name: TikTok
sites.notes: Disabled by default: TikTok aggressively fingerprints and blocks anonymous scripted clients.

sites.name: Reddit
sites.notes: Disabled by default: Reddit blocks anonymous scripted clients and now requires OAuth for its API. Review your profile while signed in, or use your own API credentials outside this tool.

sites.name: Quora
sites.notes: Disabled by default: Quora gates profiles behind a sign-in wall.

sites.name: Telegram
sites.notes: Disabled by default: t.me answers 200 for both existing and missing handles, so a status check would be a coin flip. Use Telegram's in-app search instead.

sites.name: Snapchat
sites.notes: Disabled by default: unverified, client-rendered, and rate-limited aggressively.

sites.name: VK
sites.notes: Disabled by default: VK answers 200 for unknown vanity names, so status detection does not work.

sites.name: Substack
sites.notes: Disabled by default: unverified, client-rendered. Run `d3ta1l3r calibrate --sites substack_user` and pin the answer in this file before enabling it.

sites.name: Product Hunt
sites.notes: Disabled by default: unverified signature and a client-rendered profile page.

sites.name: Flickr
sites.notes: Disabled by default: Flickr identifies people by NSID, so a vanity path is not a reliable lookup.

sites.name: Patreon
sites.notes: Disabled by default: unverified signature; Patreon serves a client-rendered shell.
